bc_boogie_man.blurb: Boogie Man is a single low boulder within the Copper Boulders zone at the foot of Copper Mountain, outside Terrace in northern British Columbia. Eight problems here are mostly easy: six sit at V0 and V1, including a traverse, and two are much harder at V4. The block is short and the ground beneath it is flat, so landings are friendly. It has no shade and takes the full sun, which makes it a good warm-up stop or a place for newer boulderers to get mileage before moving along the trail to the neighbouring boulders.

bc_pilot_s_lounge.blurb: Pilot's Lounge is a bolted sport cliff above the Mamquam forest road near Squamish, left of the Top Shelf crack wall. Eight routes are mostly in the 5.12 range, with one at 5.11 and a couple harder, including a project at the top end. The wall stands roughly 25 to 30 m tall and is described as unusually solid for the area, with pockets and pinches. It stays shaded until late afternoon, which helps on warm days. A long pitch up to a broad ledge is how you reach the base of the routes, so plan for a steep approach day.

bc_ultraviolet_cliff.blurb: Ultraviolet Cliff is a small crag beside the top station of the Sea to Sky Gondola above Squamish, with one of the shortest walks in the area. Its eight routes are mostly trad lines at 5.10 and 5.11, plus one aid line. Climbs run about 12 to 16 m, and nearly every one is vertical or gently overhanging, with several crack lines in the 5.9 to 5.10 range that are scarce around Squamish. The faces point southwest and southeast and pick up a lot of sun, so the rock dries quickly, which makes spring and fall visits workable.

bc_mycology_rock.blurb: Mycology Rock is a compact west-facing wall near Alice Lake, just north of Squamish, off the Wonderland trail. Most of the eight routes mix removable gear with bolts, with one pure sport line, and grades run from 5.10 to 5.12. The cliff is mostly overhanging, gets filtered sunlight and stays cool in hot weather. Many lines have seen very few ascents, so expect some loose rock and bring a helmet. A short, flat walk makes it among the quicker approaches in the Squamish area.
bc_mycology_rock.approach: Roughly ten minutes on flat ground from the car.

bc_rock_candy.blurb: Rock Candy is a small sport wall in Rose Valley, above the lake in West Kelowna, in the Okanagan. Eight bolted routes sit close together on technical face terrain, with grades from 5.10 up to just under 5.12 and most falling in the 5.10 to 5.11 range. One small boulder is also tucked in beside the wall. The face gets shade in the afternoon, so it suits warm days later on. The wall is named for the nearby downhill bike trail, and riders come down it at speed, so stay alert on the approach.

bc_sandy_cove.blurb: Sandy Cove is a small beach bouldering spot inside Sandy Cove Park on Marine Drive in West Vancouver, between Dundarave and Lighthouse Park. Eight problems are listed, mostly easy: around three each at V0 and V1, then one V2 and one V3, so it suits beginners and a quick session of a couple of hours. The blocks sit on the sand and can only be climbed when the tide is low or going out, so check tide times first. There is no signage at the stairs down to the beach, which makes the spot easy to miss.
bc_sandy_cove.approach: Take the stairs or short trail under the bridge down to the beach; the boulders are just to your right on the sand.
bc_sandy_cove.parking_note: Limited roadside spaces on either side of the bridge on Marine Drive; there are no signs, so it is easy to drive past.
